items.name: Phata
items.flag: Lesotho spelling is Phato; SA Sesotho Phata is fine. Also a common word (phata = to pluck/lay out), so context matters. Not a season.

items.name: Tshitwe
items.flag: Lesotho form is Tshitoe/Tšitoe; Tshitwe is the SA form. Spelling variants exist (Tshitwe/Tshitoe).

items.name: Mmesa
items.flag: Some sources spell Mmese; Mmesa is also used. Spelling not fully standardised, but no other month is plausible.

items.name: Pundungwane
items.flag: Rare long word; could be mis-typed (Pudungwane). Also possibly confused with Mphalane (Oct) by sound only.

items.name: Leotshe
items.flag: Lesotho form is Loetse; Leotshe is the SA form. Spelling variants (Leotshe/Loetse) exist.

items.name: Motsheanong
items.flag: Derived from tsheanong; a seasonal flavour (late autumn) but it is the month name, not a season.

items.name: Mphalane
items.flag: Same form used in Lesotho. No flag beyond sound similarity to Phata/Pundungwane.

items.name: Hlakola
items.flag: Easily confused with Hlakubele (March) because both start Hlak-; the short forms Hlk and Hlb must stay distinct.

items.name: Pherekgong
items.flag: Lesotho form is Phesekgong/Phesekong (Pherekgong is the SA form). Spelling variants (Pherekgong/Phirimane in other sources) exist; verify spelling.

items.name: Phupu
items.flag: Easily confused with Phupjane (June); short forms Phu and Php are close. Lesotho uses Phupu for July as well.

items.name: Hlakubele
items.flag: Confusable with Hlakola (February). Same form used in Lesotho.

items.name: Phupjane
items.flag: Lesotho form is Phupjane/Phuptjane; confusable with Phupu (July). Month assignment of Phupu vs Phupjane is the single highest swap risk.

summary: All 12 names map one-to-one onto January to December (Pherekgong 1, Hlakola 2, Hlakubele 3, Mmesa 4, Motsheanong 5, Phupjane 6, Phupu 7, Phata 8, Leotshe 9, Mphalane 10, Pundungwane 11, Tshitwe 12), with no duplicates or gaps. Main risks are the near-identical pairs Hlakola/Hlakubele and Phupu/Phupjane, plus spelling variants (Mmesa/Mmese, Leotshe/Loetse, Tshitwe/Tshitoe, Phata/Phato) where Lesotho forms differ from the South African ones. No name is a season. This is a machine review from model knowledge only, not an approval by a fluent Sesotho speaker; a native speaker should confirm spellings before shipping.
